events.text: Built the Paint Faces tool: Build menu / N key arms it; touching a placed piece's face binds the active browser material into that face's slot (per-face — front/back/top/bottom stay separate); drag sweeps, one paint per face per stroke. 7-case suite proves the hit-normal→slot-role mapping incl. the yaw-90 front/back swap.

User bounce (req_2886): painting looked like it consumed ALL faces. Root cause was NOT the slot write — pieceInstanceRows tinted every overlay box with the PRIMARY slot's colour (pieceBaseHex). Fixed in c1e13cf44: per-box colours via the shared slotRefForBox chain.

resolution: Built the Paint Faces mode the ask describes: a new armed world tool (Build menu, key N, Paintbrush icon in the action bar) where touching a placed build piece's face applies the browser's active paint/texture to THAT face's texture slot — explicitly per-face, so an exterior wall face and its interior face take different materials without fighting. The host build raycast already computed the hit face normal; it's now surfaced through the pick door, and a new faceRoleForHit maps normal+yaw to the exact slot role the skin renderer draws (walls front/back/sides incl. the quarter-turn swap, plates top/bottom/edges, single-surface kinds), proven by a 7-case test suite. Click paints, drag sweeps across faces (each face paints once per stroke), writes go through the existing assignPieceSlotAsset path so every paint is a real undo entry and feeds the RECENT materials row. Faces without texture slots (authored/model pieces, occluders) are intentional no-ops. Docs: docs/game/editor_face_paint.md + _index record (oracle-visible). Editor cart bundles clean; world suites green. Known limits noted in the doc: quarter-turn yaw assumption, one undo entry per face, authored pieces have no slots yet.
